turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_shg_eg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format), `shg` (the largest
    SHG tensor component |d_ij|, in pm/V) and `band_gap` (the band gap, in
    eV).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, select 5 candidates that jointly span the best
trade-off between a LARGE SHG tensor component |d_ij| and a WIDE band gap.
Neither is given for the pool. Your 5 picks are scored by the dominated
hypervolume they span in the normalized (|d_ij|, band gap) plane, so a set
of mutually non-dominated candidates covering the frontier beats 5
candidates that are all strong on the same single axis.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training set shows a clear inverse correlation between SHG and gap that is controlled by chemistry and local coordination. Tetrahedral (zincblende/chalcopyrite/wurtzite-derived) networks give the highest SHG once the anions become heavy and polarizable (Te, As, P), while the same networks with lighter anions (S) or more ionic cations push the gap upward at the expense of SHG. Alkali/alkaline-earth halides sit at the opposite extreme (gap > 5 eV, SHG < 1 pm V\(^{-1}\)).

Consequently the five pool structures that best reproduce these distinct regimes, and that are therefore mutually non-dominated, are:

- c073 (CdIn\(_3\)AsTe\(_4\)) – direct analogue of the training ZnIn\(_3\)AsSe\(_4\) (55 pm V\(^{-1}\), 1.32 eV) but with Te; expected to occupy the high-SHG/low-gap end of the front.
- c090 (K\(_{14}\)Ta\(_2\)As\(_8\)) – isostructural with the training K\(_{14}\)Nb\(_2\)As\(_8\) (69 pm V\(^{-1}\), 1.68 eV); places a second high-SHG point at modestly larger gap.
- c055 (Al\(_3\)Ga\(_3\)As\(_6\)) – wurtzite-derived AlGaAs superlattice, chemically intermediate between training GaP (69 pm V\(^{-1}\), 1.86 eV) and AlSb; fills the SHG \(\approx\) 60–70 pm V\(^{-1}\), gap \(\approx\) 2 eV region.
- c051 (Zn\(_2\)Ga\(_4\)S\(_8\)) – Zn analogue of training CdGa\(_2\)S\(_4\) (22 pm V\(^{-1}\), 2.86 eV); moves the front to gap \(\approx\) 3.1 eV while retaining double-digit SHG.
- c057 (Li\(_4\)Al\(_4\)S\(_8\)) – LiAlS\(_2\)-type tetrahedral sulfide, analogous to the training Li-Zn-P-S and Ba-Ga-Si-S families (SHG 8–13 pm V\(^{-1}\), gap 3.8–4.3 eV); supplies the wide-gap end of the chalcogenide front.

These five points jointly trace the empirical Pareto surface from (high \(d_{ij}\), \(E_g\sim1\) eV) to (moderate \(d_{ij}\), \(E_g\sim4\) eV) and therefore maximise dominated hypervolume.

Final: c073, c090, c055, c051, c057
